name: goap_string_domains_derived_alphabet
supersedes: spec_library/synthesized_registry/goap_string_domains_honest.meta.json (that entry hardcoded a fixed ASCII alphabet ['a','b','c'] and pre-built the full alphabet^max_len closure; this entry replaces the hardcoded alphabet with one DERIVED from the actual strings in play, and replaces the full closure with facts generated only along the actual search path, times the full derived alphabet at each step for genuine decoys)
mechanism: friendly_cli/lib/goap_string_universe.patlang v2: collect_alphabet(strings) derives the deduplicated character set actually used across a given string pool (generic extraction, not hand-picked) using len()/substr() -- both already iterate by .chars() (code points), so this needed no ASCII-specific logic. emit_targeted_concat_facts emits concat(prefix,char,prefix+char) facts ONLY for prefixes along the true path from start to target, times the FULL derived alphabet at each step -- giving genuine decoys (wrong branches dead-end one step later) with fact count linear in (target_len * alphabet_size), not exponential in alphabet_size^max_len like the v1 hardcoded-closure approach.
given_background: collect_alphabet / emit_targeted_concat_facts -- generic infrastructure, same status as pred1/succ/reach_closure elsewhere.
verification: All 5 tasks re-verified with the derived-alphabet, targeted-facts mechanism: build-from-scratch (+blind), A+B concatenation, reverse, palindrome-via-composition, and a genuine unreachable negative case ('z', outside the derived alphabet) all correct.
real_bug_discovered_while_testing_this_I: Testing intentionally included non-ASCII strings ('café', Chinese characters) to prove the derived-alphabet approach needs no special-casing for Unicode. This exposed a genuine, PRE-EXISTING PatLang lexer bug, unrelated to GOAP/synthesis work: rust-runtime/src/lexer.rs reads source text BYTE-BY-BYTE via `bytes[position] as char` (confirmed at line 216 and throughout the string-literal scan at lines 364-367+385), never decoding multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. A file containing correctly UTF-8-encoded 'café' (bytes 63 61 66 C3 A9) is lexed as 5 separate (wrong) characters instead of 4, with the multi-byte character split into mojibake fragments (each raw byte re-interpreted as its own codepoint: C3->'Ã', A9->'©'). Confirmed by direct byte-level inspection of the source file (correct on disk) versus PatLang's own len()/substr() output (corrupted at runtime). PatLang string literals containing non-ASCII text are currently unusable. This is a separate, standalone finding -- flagged to the user, not fixed as part of this GOAP work (out of scope; would need real UTF-8-aware lexing, decoding grapheme/codepoint boundaries instead of raw bytes).
provenance: direct response to: 'I feel that defining all the alphabet separately is an annoying and slightly dodgy approach, and would be troublesome if we move to unicode. Could we not, for instance, define a function which can (lazily?) generate the alphabet in use and pass that in, or otherwise avoid this sort of approach?'
